title: Quarterly scenario staging & decision cadence for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Mandel
description:
Synopsis: Establish a repeatable quarterly process that stages scenario-driven model lineup decisions (additions, deprecations, and variant rollouts) for Hosted API and the Model Catalog. The goal is a transparent decision cadence that ties to OKRs, surfaces risk early, and gives engineering predictable commit windows and rollback lanes.

Scope: Q3 planning across hosted endpoints and model catalog phasing. Includes: decision calendar, staging environments and canary windows, runway/capacity estimation for Dedicated pools, QA/eval gating for model quality regressions, and documented cross-functional sign-off steps. Out of scope: on-prem deployment packaging and enterprise contract negotiations (handled by Private team).

Success criteria: teams can declare a model lineup commitment with clear phasing and rollback timelines; fewer last-minute emergency rollbacks during the quarter; and measurable reduction in variance between planned vs actual rollout dates.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a public decision calendar for Q3 with >= 3 commit windows and associated rollback policies
Define and document a 'scenario staging' template (traffic profiles, eval prompt sets, expected latency/cost delta) and circulate to Eng/Design/R&D
Complete a dry-run of one canary window for a low-risk model variant with monitoring runbook attached
Obtain sign-off from runtime, infra, and reliability teams for capacity runway estimates before final commitment
Create a short dashboard (Console) widget showing model rollout status, canary health, and regression alerts
milestones: 2025-07-18: Scenario templates and canary playbook drafted
2025-07-30: Capacity runway estimation completed (Dedicated & Hosted burst)
2025-08-12: First dry-run canary executed and lessons captured
2025-08-28: Quarter decision calendar published and OKR sync completed
2025-09-10: Final commit window for Q3 lineup
risks: Underestimated Dedicated capacity needs leading to constrained canary windows
Eval set blind spots causing undetected quality regressions during canary
Stakeholder misalignment between Hosted API product owners and Model Ops on deprecation timing
Tooling gaps in Console to visualize per-model canary health could slow review cycles
